credit_unions.name: Navy Federal Credit Union

fom.summary: Active duty, retired, and veteran members of all branches of the armed forces, Department of Defense civilian employees and contractors, and immediate family and household members of any of the above. Family eligibility extends broadly — parents, grandparents, siblings, children, and grandchildren of someone eligible can all join.
fom.easy_path: If anyone in your family ever served in the military, you almost certainly qualify through them — even if they never joined Navy Federal themselves.
fom.join_cost: $5 minimum deposit to a savings account

products.checking: Free Active Duty and Free EveryDay checking with no monthly fees; early direct deposit for military pay
products.savings: Basic savings plus money market accounts; certificate specials are the standout
products.cds: Certificates from 3 months to 7 years, including frequent limited-time special rates and a low-minimum EasyStart certificate
products.loans: Consistently low auto loan rates, VA home loans with no PMI, and credit cards with below-average APR ranges

credit_unions.rates_note: Certificate specials and auto loan rates regularly beat national bank averages; verify current APYs on navyfederal.org before deciding.
pros: Largest credit union in the country with 350+ branches, many on or near bases worldwide
Certificate specials and auto rates regularly among the best available anywhere
Very generous family eligibility — one veteran in the family tree can unlock membership for many relatives
24/7 phone support staffed for military time zones
cons: No path to membership without a military or DoD connection
Savings account base rate is unremarkable — the good yields are in certificates
So large that service can feel like a big bank at times
editorial: Navy Federal is the credit union most Americans have actually heard of, and for good reason: it is roughly three times the size of its nearest competitor and behaves like a full-service national bank that happens to return its profits to members. For military families it is close to a default choice — early pay deposit, base-adjacent branches, and lending products built around deployment realities like the Servicemembers Civil Relief Act.

The catch is the front door. Navy Federal has no donation workaround, no association membership trick, and no open charter. You either have a military or DoD connection — including through immediate family — or you don't get in. Before assuming you're excluded, though, walk your family tree: a parent or grandparent who served is enough, and household members of eligible people also qualify.

Where Navy Federal earns its reputation is pricing on the products that matter. Its certificate specials routinely top national leaderboards, its auto loans undercut most banks, and its credit cards carry APR ranges capped below the industry norm of 29%-plus. If you qualify, it belongs on your shortlist even if you keep another credit union for daily banking.
credit_unions.best_for: Military members, veterans, and their extended families

credit_unions.name: State Employees' Credit Union (SECU)

fom.summary: Employees of NC state government and related entities (public school boards, certain county departments, state employee associations), NC National Guard; retirees/pensioners/annuitants of those employers; immediate family and household members of members; un-remarried surviving spouses; active and former employees of Blue Cross Blue Shield of NC and listed related organizations.
fom.join_cost: $25 minimum deposit to a share account

products.checking: Single no-frills checking account with a flat $1 monthly fee and unusually low overdraft costs
products.savings: Share and money market accounts with consistently fair, if not chart-topping, yields
products.cds: Share term certificates with straightforward terms and no gimmick tiers
products.loans: Low-cost mortgages serviced in-house, auto loans, and a salary advance loan designed to replace payday lending

credit_unions.rates_note: SECU competes on low fees and honest loan pricing more than on headline APYs; verify current rates at ncsecu.org.
pros: Second-largest credit union in the US with a branch in every North Carolina county
A salary advance loan that is a genuine payday-loan alternative, not a fee trap
In-house mortgage servicing — your loan is never sold
Famously low and simple fee schedule
cons: Membership is strictly tied to NC public employment and family — no workaround
Technology and app experience lag the big national players
Deposit rates are fair rather than market-leading
editorial: SECU is what people imagine when they picture a credit union doing right by its members: a branch in all 100 North Carolina counties, a $1 checking account, and a salary advance product that exists specifically to keep state employees away from payday lenders. It is a deeply mission-driven institution that has resisted the temptation to chase growth outside its charter.

That discipline cuts both ways. There is no donation trick or association membership that gets an outsider in — if you are not connected to North Carolina public employment or to a current member's family, SECU is simply not available to you. And members occasionally grumble that the technology feels a generation behind Navy Federal or Alliant.

For those who do qualify, the value is in the totality: low fees, fair loan pricing, mortgages that are never sold to a servicer you didn't choose, and physical access everywhere in the state. It is less a rate-shopper's credit union than a keep-everything-here credit union.
credit_unions.best_for: North Carolina public employees and their families

credit_unions.name: PenFed Credit Union

fom.summary: Open to everyone. PenFed dropped its military-affiliation requirement in 2019 — any US citizen or permanent resident can join by opening a savings account with $5.
fom.easy_path: Just open a $5 savings account during the application. No donation, no association fee, no military connection needed.

products.checking: Free checking plus an interest-bearing Access America checking tier
products.savings: Premium Online Savings with rates competitive with online banks
products.cds: Money market certificates from 6 months to 7 years, frequently near the top of national rate tables
products.loans: Strong auto loan pricing, mortgages including VA loans, personal loans, and well-regarded rewards credit cards

credit_unions.rates_note: PenFed's online savings and certificates are priced to compete with online banks, not local branches; verify current APYs at penfed.org.
pros: Anyone in the US can join — one of the largest truly open credit unions
Certificate and online savings rates that compete with internet banks
Full product shelf: mortgages, autos, cards, personal loans
Heritage of serving military members without requiring military ties
cons: Branch network is thin outside the DC area and a few markets
Customer service reviews are mixed, especially for lending
Checking rates require direct deposit to hit the advertised tier
editorial: PenFed is the easiest answer to the most common credit union question: 'can I even join one?' Since 2019 the answer here is yes, full stop — a $5 savings deposit makes anyone a member. That open door, combined with online-bank-grade deposit rates, makes PenFed the default national pick for people who don't have a local credit union connection.

Functionally, PenFed behaves like a hybrid of an online bank and a traditional credit union. Its money market certificates and Premium Online Savings are priced against Marcus and Ally rather than against the bank branch on the corner, and its credit cards — particularly the Pathfinder and Power Cash Rewards lines — are competitive with major issuers.

The trade-off is service depth. Branches are sparse unless you live near Washington, DC, and member reviews of loan servicing are noticeably more mixed than at smaller credit unions. Treat PenFed as a rate-driven national institution rather than a relationship-driven local one and you'll calibrate your expectations correctly.
credit_unions.best_for: Anyone, anywhere in the US, who wants top-tier rates

fom.summary: Current and retired employees of California public and private schools, colleges, and education-related organizations, plus immediate family members of existing members.

pros: Largest education-focused credit union in the country
Products genuinely built around educator pay cycles (summer saver, paycheck planning)
Very low fee schedule and free checking
cons: Limited to the California education community and their families
Deposit rates are good, not national-leaderboard material
editorial: SchoolsFirst is the country's largest education-sector credit union and one of the clearest examples of a niche charter done well. Its product design assumes you get paid ten months a year: summer saver accounts smooth income across the gap, and its planning tools are built for school-district pay calendars rather than retrofitted from generic bank products.

Membership is genuinely restricted — you need a connection to California education, either directly or through family. There is no donation path. But the definition is broader than 'teacher': classified staff, college employees, school vendors' staff in some cases, and retirees all count, and one family member unlocks eligibility for the rest.

Member satisfaction surveys routinely place SchoolsFirst near the top of all US financial institutions, which matters more here than headline APY. If you're a California educator choosing between this and a megabank, the fee schedule alone usually settles the argument.
credit_unions.best_for: California school employees and their families

credit_unions.name: BECU (Boeing Employees' Credit Union)

fom.summary: Anyone who lives, works, worships, or attends school in Washington state or select Idaho and Oregon counties; Boeing employees anywhere; and members of partner associations.
fom.easy_path: Washington residency is the wide-open door — no employer connection needed despite the name.
fom.join_cost: $10 minimum deposit online (no deposit required in person)

credit_unions.rates_note: The boosted rate on the first $500 of savings is unusually generous for small balances; verify current tiers at becu.org.
pros: Open to all Washington residents, not just Boeing employees
Boosted first-dollar savings rate is great for people starting to save
Largest credit union in the Pacific Northwest
cons: Name still confuses people into thinking it's Boeing-only

Best rates cap out at low balance tiers
editorial: BECU's name is its biggest marketing problem: most Washingtonians don't realize that 'Boeing Employees' Credit Union' has been open to every resident of the state for years. It is now the largest credit union in the Northwest and one of the largest in the country, with a charter that requires nothing more than living, working, or studying in Washington.

Its signature move is paying a meaningfully elevated APY on the first $500 in savings and checking through Member Advantage. Rate chasers with six figures will find better homes for bulk cash, but for someone building a first emergency fund, earning a top-tier rate on early dollars is a genuinely member-first design choice.

BECU runs lean on branches and pushes members toward shared branching, ATMs, and digital channels — closer to an online bank with local roots than a branch-on-every-corner institution. Pair that with consistently low loan pricing and it's the obvious first stop for anyone banking in Washington.
credit_unions.best_for: Washington residents and Pacific Northwest savers

credit_unions.name: Golden 1 Credit Union

fom.summary: All Californians — anyone who lives or works in California can join, plus family members of existing members regardless of location.
fom.easy_path: California residency alone qualifies you; one of the simplest large-CU charters in the country.

products.checking: Free checking with early direct deposit
products.savings: Standard share savings plus a high-yield online savings tier
products.cds: Term certificates with occasional promotional specials
products.loans: Auto loans are the franchise product, with first-time buyer programs; also mortgages and HELOCs

credit_unions.rates_note: Auto loan pricing is the standout; deposit rates are mid-pack for California; verify at golden1.com.
pros: Open to every California resident with 70+ branches statewide
Strong auto lending program including first-time buyer options
Free checking with early payday deposit
Naming-rights visibility (Golden 1 Center) reflects a stable, large institution
cons: Digital experience is functional but not class-leading
Branch coverage thins outside major metro areas
editorial: Golden 1 is California's everyman credit union: no employer requirement, no association dues, just proof you live or work in the state. With more than a million members and branches from Redding to San Diego, it functions as a statewide community bank that happens to be member-owned.

Its center of gravity is auto lending. Golden 1 consistently prices new and used auto loans below California bank averages and runs first-time buyer programs that are friendlier than dealer financing for thin-credit borrowers. If you walk into a California dealership, the rate you bring from Golden 1 is a strong negotiating baseline.

On the deposit side it is solid rather than spectacular — the online savings tier helps, but rate maximizers will pair Golden 1 with an internet bank. Think of it as the relationship hub for Californians: checking, auto loan, branch access, with overflow savings parked wherever yields are highest.
credit_unions.best_for: California residents, especially auto loan shoppers

credit_unions.name: America First Credit Union

fom.summary: Anyone who lives, works, worships, attends school, or volunteers in qualifying areas of Utah, Nevada, Arizona, Idaho, Oregon, New Mexico, and part of San Bernardino County, California, plus immediate family or household of existing members, the Utah food industry, and Select Employer Groups.

credit_unions.rates_note: Certificate flexibility (bump and add-on options) is a differentiator; verify current APYs at americafirst.com.
pros: $1 membership deposit and broad six-state eligibility
Add-on and bump-rate certificates are unusually flexible
Strong auto loan rates across the Mountain West
Large branch and ATM network in Utah and Nevada
cons: No path to join from outside the six-state footprint
Base savings rate is low — yields live in certificates

editorial: America First is the Mountain West's dominant credit union, with a footprint spanning six states and a $1 membership share that makes it one of the cheapest financial institutions in America to join. In Utah it is functionally a default banking choice, with branch density rivaling any bank.

Its most underrated products are its flexible certificates. Add-on certificates let you keep contributing after opening — rare in the industry and ideal for savers building toward a goal at a locked rate — while bump options hedge against rising rates. For disciplined savers this flexibility can beat a slightly higher headline APY elsewhere.

Auto lending is the other pillar, with pricing that consistently undercuts regional banks. The main limitation is simply geography: live outside the six-state zone with no qualifying family member, and America First is off the table.
credit_unions.best_for: Mountain West residents and certificate ladder builders

credit_unions.name: Alliant Credit Union

fom.summary: Employees/retirees of partner businesses, immediate family or domestic partners of members, people who live or work in eligible communities near Chicago HQ; anyone else can select 'Other: Join Alliant Credit Union Foundation' and the Foundation pays the one-time $5 membership fee.
fom.easy_path: Anyone can join: select 'Other: Join Alliant Credit Union Foundation' during the application; the Foundation pays the one-time $5 membership fee.
fom.join_cost: $5 minimum deposit (association fee paid by Alliant)

products.cds: Certificates from 3 months to 5 years with low $1,000 minimums
products.loans: Auto loans, personal loans, and a flat-rate cash-back credit card

credit_unions.rates_note: Alliant prices deposits against online banks, not branch banks; verify current APYs at alliantcreditunion.org.
pros: Effectively open to anyone in the US — Alliant even pays the qualifying association fee
High-yield savings and checking rates that compete with the best online banks
No overdraft fees and generous ATM rebates
cons: Fully digital — no branch network at all
Deposit-focused; lending menu is thinner than full-service rivals
Phone support hours, while decent, aren't 24/7 for everything
editorial: Alliant is the credit union for people who would otherwise pick an online bank. It has no branches, a first-rate app, savings yields that track the national online-bank leaders, and a checking account that rebates ATM fees and refuses to charge overdrafts. The cooperative structure is almost invisible in daily use — in the best way.

Joining is deliberately frictionless: if you lack a geographic or employer connection, you select 'Other: Join Alliant Credit Union Foundation' during signup and the Foundation pays the one-time $5 membership fee. That makes it, alongside PenFed and Connexus, one of the truly national 'anyone can join' credit unions — and the most digitally polished of the group.

What Alliant is not is a lending powerhouse. Mortgages were discontinued, and the product shelf is intentionally narrow. The play here is simple: use Alliant as your high-yield hub for savings and fee-free checking, and shop loans wherever pricing is best.
credit_unions.best_for: Digital-first savers anywhere in the US

credit_unions.name: Mountain America Credit Union

fom.summary: People who live, work, worship, or attend school in qualifying areas of Utah, Idaho, Montana, Arizona, Nevada, and New Mexico; employees of select groups; and family of members. Membership in a partner association can also qualify residents of its footprint states.
fom.easy_path: Within its six-state footprint, association membership (small one-time fee) covers nearly everyone who doesn't otherwise qualify.
fom.join_cost: $1 minimum deposit; small association fee if joining that way

products.checking: Free and rewards checking tiers
products.savings: Share savings, money markets, and frequent certificate specials
products.cds: Term deposits with regular promotional rates
products.loans: Full-spectrum lender: autos, RVs, mortgages, business loans, and credit cards

credit_unions.rates_note: Certificate specials are frequently competitive regionally; verify current offers at macu.com.
pros: Fast-growing, full-service lender with strong business banking for a credit union
Broad Mountain West eligibility with an association fallback
cons: Aggressive growth means a more sales-forward culture than typical credit unions
Outside the Mountain West there's no way in
Fee schedule is longer than minimalist rivals like Alliant
editorial: Mountain America is the fastest-growing of the big Mountain West credit unions and the most commercially ambitious — it advertises heavily, opens branches aggressively, and runs a business-banking operation that rivals community banks. Members get a full-service institution that doesn't make you go elsewhere for any major product.

That ambition shows up in the member experience both ways. The technology and branch coverage are excellent, and its certificate specials are genuinely worth tracking. But the culture is more sales-oriented than the sleepy local CU stereotype — expect to be offered products. Eligibility is broad within Utah, Idaho, Montana, Arizona, Nevada, and New Mexico, including an association route, but it remains a regional institution by design.
credit_unions.best_for: Mountain West households wanting one full-service institution

credit_unions.name: Randolph-Brooks Federal Credit Union (RBFCU)

fom.summary: People who live, work, worship, attend school, or volunteer in qualifying Texas counties (covering San Antonio, Austin, Dallas-Fort Worth and beyond), employees of select groups, military connections, and family of members.
fom.easy_path: The county list covers most of urban Texas — check the map before assuming you're out.

products.savings: Share savings and money markets
products.cds: Standard certificate menu with member-friendly minimums
products.loans: Texas-leading auto rates, mortgages, and a 2%-cash-back credit card with no annual fee

credit_unions.rates_note: Auto pricing and the no-annual-fee cash-back card are the headline products; checking pays only a token APY. Verify rates at rbfcu.org.
pros: Free checking with no minimum balance games
CashBack Rewards card pays a flat 2% with no annual fee — rare at any institution
Consistently low Texas auto loan pricing
cons: Eligibility is Texas-centric; no national path
Branch network concentrated along the I-35 corridor
editorial: RBFCU is the strongest argument in Texas for ditching a megabank. Its free checking has no hoops (though it pays only a token rate), and its no-annual-fee credit card pays a flat 2% back — a combination that simply doesn't exist at Chase or Bank of America. Add auto loan pricing that consistently leads the Texas market and the everyday-banking case writes itself.

Eligibility looks restrictive on paper but covers most of urban Texas in practice — the qualifying county list spans San Antonio, Austin, and the DFW metroplex. Outside Texas, though, there's no association workaround, which keeps RBFCU a regional story. For Texans, it's arguably the best all-around value in the state.
credit_unions.best_for: Texans who want free checking, sharp auto loans and a cash-back card

fom.summary: Anyone who lives, works, attends school, or worships in most of the Florida peninsula's counties (40+ counties on the Gulf side and central Florida), plus family of members and alumni of Florida College campuses in the area.

editorial: Suncoast is Florida's hometown giant — the state's largest credit union, grown out of Tampa's teacher community into a 40-plus-county institution covering most of the peninsula. Its community identity is unusually concrete: every debit card swipe sends money to local education foundations, a program that has funneled tens of millions of dollars to Florida schools.

For members, the standout economics are on the borrowing side. Its auto pricing is consistently sharp, though its credit card APRs (now from 15.75%) no longer stand out. Deposit rates are unremarkable, so the optimal play for Floridians is Suncoast for checking and auto loans, with bulk savings wherever yields lead.
credit_unions.best_for: Florida peninsula residents, especially auto borrowers

editorial: Merger update: First Tech and Digital Federal Credit Union (DCU) legally merged on January 1, 2026 into one credit union, First Technology Federal Credit Union (NCUA charter #23521, per First Tech's merger notice). First Tech and DCU still operate as separate divisions with their own websites, accounts and rates during integration, so this review covers the First Tech division; see our DCU review for the other. Because both are now one insured institution, NCUA coverage of $250,000 per ownership category applies to your First Tech and DCU deposits combined.

First Tech built its franchise inside the badge gates of Microsoft, Intel, and HP, and it remains the credit union that best understands technology compensation. If your income arrives as salary plus RSUs, First Tech's mortgage and personal-loan underwriting will read your pay stub correctly — something megabanks still fumble.

What most people miss is that you don't need a tech employer to join: a one-time Computer History Museum or Financial Fitness Association membership, handled during the application, opens the door to anyone in the country. That puts First Tech on the short national list of effectively open credit unions, alongside PenFed, Alliant, and Connexus.

Day to day it behaves like a competent digital-first institution with West Coast and (through DCU) New England branches. Its current Rewards Checking pays only a token rate, so don't choose it for checking yield. The reason to choose First Tech is lending sophistication, not deposit yield.
credit_unions.best_for: Tech workers and anyone wanting an open-membership lender

editorial: VyStar grew from Jacksonville's military base credit union into a million-member institution spanning 76 counties across two states. It pairs free everyday banking with one of the more serious business-lending operations among US credit unions — a genuine option for Southeast small businesses that feel unloved by regional banks.

Honesty requires mentioning the 2022 digital banking conversion, which locked members out of online access for days and drew regulatory attention. The systems have long since stabilized, but it remains a cautionary data point about fast-growing credit unions outrunning their infrastructure. Members today get a solid, fair-priced regional institution with deep community roots in north Florida.
credit_unions.best_for: North Florida and south Georgia households and small businesses

editorial: Security Service is, above all, an auto lender wearing a credit union charter. Born at Kelly Air Force Base, it now finances cars at scale across Texas, Colorado, and Utah, often directly through dealerships — there's a fair chance a Texan reading this has been offered SSFCU financing at a dealer without realizing it. Its dealer-channel pricing is consistently among the region's sharpest.

As a primary banking relationship it's competent but unspectacular: free checking, ordinary savings rates, decent certificates. The smart use case is targeted — join for the auto loan when you're in one of its metros, keep it if the everyday banking suits you.

editorial: Merger update: DCU and First Tech Federal Credit Union legally merged on January 1, 2026 into one credit union, First Technology Federal Credit Union (NCUA charter #23521, per First Tech's merger notice). DCU still runs as a separate division with its own website, accounts and rates while the two integrate, so this review covers DCU's products as offered today; see our First Tech review for the other division. Because both divisions are now one insured institution, NCUA coverage of $250,000 per ownership category applies to your DCU and First Tech deposits combined, not separately.

DCU was 'digital-first' before the term existed — chartered in 1979 to serve Digital Equipment Corporation and now a nationwide, million-member institution that anyone can join with a small one-time charity donation. Its calling card is the Primary Savings rate: an APY on the first $1,000 that typically multiples the national average, making it a favorite first account for kids, students, and emergency-fund starters.

Beyond the headline perk, DCU is a workmanlike national lender — auto loans priced aggressively in all 50 states, fair mortgages, free checking. Its lending menu is tuned to Southern California reality, with jumbo mortgages and HELOCs sized for seven-figure housing stock. Eligibility now covers nine Southern California counties, and anyone elsewhere can qualify through the $8 Financial Fitness Association path — though its branch network keeps SDCCU a regional choice. Patelco provided credit monitoring, restored accounts, and rebuilt its security stack; members today bank at an institution that learned that lesson expensively. Service is adequate rather than luxurious, and the checking APY demands monthly activity. fom.easy_path: Indiana residency alone qualifies you.

credit_unions.products_brief: Indiana's largest CU, open to nearly all Hoosiers, with full lending and a wide branch network.
credit_unions.blurb: Indiana's largest credit union, renamed Everwise in 2023, long ago opened beyond educators — nearly any Hoosier can join (in Marion County, only certain townships qualify). Its statewide branch network and full lending menu make it Indiana's broadest cooperative answer to regional banks.
pros: Open to nearly all Indiana residents
Largest CU branch network in the state
cons: Marion County eligibility limited to certain townships

credit_unions.name: Elements Financial Federal Credit Union

fom.summary: Employees of Eli Lilly and 200+ partner organizations — or anyone in the US via free membership in TruDirection, a financial-wellness association Elements sponsors.
fom.easy_path: Anyone can join: select the TruDirection association during the online application at no cost.

credit_unions.products_brief: Lilly-born CU with nationwide open membership, high-yield checking, and HSA expertise.
credit_unions.blurb: Elements began as Eli Lilly's credit union and quietly became one of the easiest CUs in America to join — its sponsored TruDirection association is free and open nationwide. Health savings accounts and high-rate checking are its specialties.
pros: Free association path open to anyone in the US
cons: Top checking rate has activity requirements

credit_unions.name: CEFCU (Citizens Equity First Credit Union)

fom.summary: Anyone who lives or works in 32 qualifying central Illinois counties, or lives, works or worships in Alameda, Contra Costa or Santa Clara County, California; Caterpillar and CEFCU partner-company employees and retirees; ISU Alumni Association or ISU Athletic Boosters members; plus immediate family and household members.
fom.easy_path: Central Illinois residency qualifies you.

credit_unions.products_brief: Caterpillar-born CU with excellent loan pricing and an odd-couple Illinois/Silicon Valley footprint.
credit_unions.blurb: CEFCU grew up with Caterpillar in Peoria and remains downstate Illinois' dominant cooperative, with a quirky second home in San Jose from Cat's old plant. Loan pricing — autos and mortgages — is consistently among Illinois' best.
cons: Eligibility limited to two distant regions

credit_unions.name: Meritrust Credit Union

fom.summary: Anyone who lives, works, worships or attends school in Meritrust's Wichita- and Lawrence-area expansion areas in Kansas or in 20 qualifying Colorado counties (Denver/Boulder/Front Range and more), employees of 750+ partner companies and organizations, and family of members. Anyone else can join through a complimentary partner-association membership.
fom.easy_path: Anyone can join through a complimentary partner-association membership; local paths cover the Wichita and Lawrence areas and 20 Colorado counties.
fom.join_cost: $5 membership savings deposit; partner association membership complimentary

credit_unions.products_brief: Kansas–Colorado CU with an open association path, free checking, and aircraft-industry roots.
credit_unions.blurb: Born among Wichita's aircraft workers, Meritrust now serves the Wichita and Lawrence areas of Kansas and 20 Colorado counties after combining with Premier Members, and anyone can join through a complimentary partner-association membership. Free checking and competitive auto loans anchor a straightforward lineup.
pros: Anyone can join through a free partner-association membership
cons: Branches limited to Kansas and Colorado
credit_unions.best_for: Kansas and Front Range Colorado residents

credit_unions.name: CommunityAmerica Credit Union

fom.summary: Employees of 1,100+ partner companies and their families, people who live or work in select qualified-community ZIP codes (Kansas City area, Northwest Arkansas, and parts of Southern California), family of members, and anyone who joins the nonprofit Friends of Hobbs (free registration).
fom.easy_path: Anyone can join: CommunityAmerica registers you with Friends of Hobbs at no cost.

credit_unions.products_brief: Kansas City's hometown CU with profit-sharing payouts and Chiefs-partnership visibility.
credit_unions.blurb: CommunityAmerica is Kansas City's cooperative flagship, famous locally for annual profit-sharing checks to members and its Patrick Mahomes ad campaigns. Kansas City–area residents on both sides of the state line qualify, and anyone else can join through free Friends of Hobbs registration.
cons: Branches concentrated in the KC metro
Headline rates are average between payouts

credit_unions.name: Abound Credit Union

fom.summary: Anyone who lives, works, or attends school in dozens of central Kentucky counties, Fort Knox personnel, and family of members.
fom.easy_path: Central Kentucky residency qualifies most in the region.

credit_unions.products_brief: Kentucky's largest CU, Fort Knox-born, with strong CDs and military-friendly service.
credit_unions.blurb: Formerly Fort Knox Federal, Abound is Kentucky's largest credit union and frequently posts the state's best certificate rates. Its military heritage shows in fee-light accounts and deployment-aware service.

credit_unions.name: Pelican Credit Union (formerly Pelican State Credit Union)

fom.summary: Anyone who lives in 25 qualifying south and central Louisiana parishes (including East Baton Rouge, Lafayette, Calcasieu, St. Tammany), employees/retirees of partner organizations, and Pelican CU employees and their family.
fom.easy_path: Residency in 25 south/central Louisiana parishes, including Baton Rouge, Lafayette and Lake Charles areas.
fom.join_cost: $10 to open ($5 membership fee + $5 minimum balance)

credit_unions.products_brief: Louisiana's broadest CU with credit-building products and in-house financial counselors.
credit_unions.blurb: Pelican State covers most Louisiana parishes and distinguishes itself with certified financial counselors on staff and genuine credit-rebuilder products — a consumer-advocate institution in a state that needs them.
pros: On-staff financial counselors free to members
cons: Small asset base limits rate competitiveness

credit_unions.name: Atlantic Federal Credit Union

fom.summary: Anyone who lives, works, worships, or attends school in Maine's qualifying counties, plus family of members.
fom.easy_path: Southern and midcoast Maine residency qualifies you.

credit_unions.products_brief: Midcoast Maine cooperative with classic community-CU service and fair loans.
credit_unions.blurb: Atlantic FCU, born at Brunswick Naval Air Station, serves southern and midcoast Maine with the small-cooperative basics done well: free checking, fair auto loans, and human-scale service.

credit_unions.name: SECU of Maryland

fom.summary: Maryland state employees (current, former, retired), employees of 1,950+ partner employers and state-funded organizations, students/alumni/staff of University System of Maryland and other listed schools, Anne Arundel County employees, and family/household members. Anyone else can qualify with a one-time donation of $10+ to the SECU MD Foundation.
fom.easy_path: Anyone can qualify with a one-time $10+ donation to the SECU MD Foundation; University System of Maryland ties also qualify.
fom.join_cost: $10 minimum share balance; $10+ one-time SECU MD Foundation donation if no other connection

credit_unions.products_brief: Maryland's largest state-chartered CU serving public employees and university communities.
credit_unions.blurb: SECU of Maryland anchors the state's public workforce and university communities — Terps alumni qualify, which captures a huge population. Free checking and fair mortgage pricing lead the menu.
cons: General-public path requires a one-time $10+ SECU MD Foundation donation
credit_unions.best_for: Maryland public employees and UMD alumni

credit_unions.name: Andrews Federal Credit Union

fom.summary: Military and civilian personnel at supported installations, DC residents, employees of partner groups — or anyone in the US via free membership in the American Consumer Council during the application.
fom.easy_path: Anyone can join: select American Consumer Council membership (free) when applying online.

credit_unions.products_brief: Military-rooted CU open to everyone via ACC, with nationally competitive certificate specials.
credit_unions.blurb: Andrews Federal serves joint-base communities from DC to Germany, but its certificates regularly hit national best-of lists — and anyone in the US can join through a free American Consumer Council membership baked into the application.
pros: Free ACC path opens membership nationwide
cons: Branches limited to DC region and bases
Digital experience is serviceable, not slick

credit_unions.name: Metro Credit Union

fom.summary: Anyone who lives, works, goes to school or has a business in 11 Massachusetts counties (Essex, Middlesex, Norfolk, Suffolk, Worcester, Plymouth, Barnstable, Bristol, Franklin, Hampshire, Hampden) or 5 southern New Hampshire counties (Hillsborough, Rockingham, Cheshire, Merrimack, Strafford), employees of about 1,800 Metro@work employers, plus family of members wherever they live.
fom.easy_path: Greater Boston residency qualifies you.

credit_unions.products_brief: Greater Boston's largest state-chartered CU with competitive CDs and free checking.
credit_unions.blurb: Metro is greater Boston's biggest state-chartered credit union, pairing genuinely competitive certificate rates with free checking in one of America's most expensive banking markets.
pros: Free checking in a high-fee market
cons: Branch network is modest for its size

credit_unions.name: Michigan State University Federal Credit Union (MSUFCU)

fom.summary: MSU and Oakland University faculty, employees, students and alumni; Cooley Law School (Lansing) employees/students; anyone who lives, works, worships or attends school in the state of Michigan; Select Employee Group employees; MSUFCU Desk Drawer Foundation donors ($10 minimum donation); and immediate family/household members.
fom.easy_path: Anyone who lives, works, worships or attends school in Michigan qualifies; MSU/OU alumni anywhere also qualify.

credit_unions.products_brief: The largest university-based credit union in the world; award-winning app and student-friendly products.
credit_unions.blurb: MSUFCU is the world's largest university credit union, with a top-rated mobile app and a product set built for students through alumni. Spartan ties anywhere in the country qualify you.
pros: Best-in-class mobile banking for a CU

credit_unions.name: DFCU Financial

fom.summary: Anyone who lives, works, or worships in Michigan's Lower Peninsula or select Florida counties, plus family of members.
fom.easy_path: Lower Peninsula residency qualifies any Michigander.

credit_unions.products_brief: Ford-born CU famous for one of the largest annual cash-back dividends in the industry.
credit_unions.blurb: DFCU Financial, born at Ford, pays members a special patronage dividend — a cash payout that has totaled over half a billion dollars since 2006, among the industry's most generous. Any Lower Peninsula Michigander can join.
pros: Long-running annual cash dividend to members
Open to all Lower Peninsula residents
cons: Everyday rates are ordinary — the dividend is the deal

credit_unions.name: Wings Credit Union

fom.summary: Aviation/air-transportation industry employees nationwide; anyone who lives or works in eligible Minnesota or Wisconsin counties or the Seattle-Tacoma, Detroit, Orlando or Atlanta metros (Colorado residents join via legacy Ent); immediate family of members; or anyone via a $5+ donation to the Wings Financial Foundation.
fom.easy_path: Anyone can join: a $5 one-time foundation donation during the application qualifies you nationwide.
fom.join_cost: $5 deposit + $5 one-time foundation donation if needed

credit_unions.products_brief: Aviation-industry CU with nationwide open path, strong CDs, and fee-light accounts.
credit_unions.blurb: Wings began with Northwest Airlines workers and still serves aviation nationwide, but a $5 foundation donation opens membership to anyone. Its certificates and money markets frequently lead the Minnesota market, and fees are scarce. On January 1, 2026 it combined with Colorado's Ent Credit Union; the merged Wings Credit Union's headquarters of record is Colorado Springs.
pros: Strong CD and money market pricing
cons: Branches limited to Minnesota/Wisconsin, Colorado, and a few other metros
Aviation branding obscures its open membership
credit_unions.best_for: Twin Cities savers and aviation workers

credit_unions.name: Affinity Plus Federal Credit Union

fom.summary: Minnesota state employees, U of M community, residents of many Minnesota communities — or anyone via a one-time $25 donation to the Affinity Plus Foundation.
fom.easy_path: Anyone can join: the $25 foundation donation option in the application covers all comers.
fom.join_cost: $10 share + $25 one-time donation if joining via foundation

credit_unions.products_brief: Member-obsessed Minnesota CU with superb service ratings and full digital banking.
credit_unions.blurb: Affinity Plus consistently posts some of the highest member-satisfaction scores of any US financial institution, and a $25 foundation donation lets anyone in the country join. Products are fair across the board; service is the star.
cons: $25 join cost is higher than peer workarounds
Rates are fair rather than leading
credit_unions.best_for: Service-first members in Minnesota and beyond

credit_unions.name: Keesler Federal Credit Union

fom.summary: Anyone who lives, works, worships, or attends school in qualifying Mississippi Gulf Coast counties and Louisiana/Alabama border areas, Keesler AFB personnel, and family of members.
fom.easy_path: Gulf Coast residency covers most of south Mississippi.

credit_unions.products_brief: Mississippi's largest CU with Gulf Coast dominance and frequent CD specials.
credit_unions.blurb: Keesler Federal, rooted at the Biloxi air base, is Mississippi's largest credit union and the Gulf Coast's financial cooperative anchor, known for aggressive certificate specials and military-grade service culture.

credit_unions.name: Hope Credit Union

fom.summary: Individuals and businesses in the Deep South communities HOPE serves (Alabama, Arkansas, Georgia, Louisiana, Mississippi, Tennessee); membership is open to those who join Hope Enterprise Corporation (via the single application), and people outside the service area can join by opening a savings, certificate or money market account.
fom.easy_path: Anyone can join: a one-time $10 membership fee (of which $5 is a contribution to Hope Enterprise Corporation) opens membership.
fom.join_cost: $10 membership fee ($5 of it goes to Hope Enterprise Corporation) + initial deposit

credit_unions.products_brief: Mission-driven CDFI credit union financing underserved Deep South communities; deposits open nationwide.
credit_unions.blurb: Hope is a community-development credit union channeling deposits into Black-majority and underbanked Deep South towns that banks abandoned. Anyone nationwide can join and hold insured savings that funds that mission — impact banking with NCUA protection.
pros: Open nationwide via small association fee

credit_unions.name: Together Credit Union

fom.summary: Anyone who lives or works in St. Louis City/County, St. Charles or Jefferson counties (MO), Madison or St. Clair counties (IL), the Williamsburg, VA area, or the Dallas, TX metro (within 10 miles of Cedar Hill plus listed ZIPs); employees of 200+ employer partners including Anheuser-Busch and its distributors; and family of members.
fom.easy_path: St. Louis metro residency qualifies you.

credit_unions.products_brief: The former Anheuser-Busch employees' CU, now metro-wide with free checking and fair lending.
credit_unions.blurb: Born inside Anheuser-Busch, Together Credit Union now serves the whole St. Louis metro on both riverbanks. It's a steady, fee-light primary-banking option with brewery-era loyalty in its DNA.
pros: Both MO and IL sides of metro qualify

credit_unions.name: Whitefish Credit Union

fom.summary: People who live, work, own property, worship, belong to an association or attend school within 50 air miles of Whitefish, MT or in eligible Montana counties (site lists Flathead, Lake, Lincoln, Sanders, Missoula, Ravalli, Lewis and Clark, Broadwater, Gallatin; a July 2025 expansion added 16 more, ~25 counties / ~85% of Montana's population), plus immediate family.
fom.easy_path: Residents of most of western and central Montana (eligible counties, ~85% of the state's population) qualify.

credit_unions.products_brief: Montana's largest credit union: broad western and central Montana eligibility, land-loan expertise, no-fee culture.
credit_unions.blurb: Whitefish CU is Montana's biggest cooperative and one of its most distinctive lenders — it understands raw land, ranch, and rural property loans that coastal banks won't touch. Eligibility covers much of western and central Montana.
pros: Eligibility across much of western and central Montana
Rare expertise in land and rural lending
credit_unions.best_for: Western and central Montanans, especially rural borrowers

credit_unions.name: Centris Federal Credit Union

fom.summary: Anyone who lives, works, worships or attends school in Cass, Dodge, Douglas, Sarpy, Saunders, Lincoln, McPherson or Washington counties (NE) or Harrison, Mills or Pottawattamie counties (IA); employees of listed Grand Island employers; and immediate family/household members.
fom.easy_path: Omaha-area residency qualifies you.

credit_unions.products_brief: Omaha's leading CU with free checking, solid autos, and business banking.
credit_unions.blurb: Centris is greater Omaha's homegrown credit union, a practical full-service alternative to the region's banks with free checking and a growing small-business operation.
pros: Business banking for a mid-size CU

credit_unions.name: Greater Nevada Credit Union (now a division of America First)

fom.summary: Anyone who lives, works, worships, volunteers or attends school in Nevada or in eligible communities in six neighboring states, plus immediate family of members.
fom.easy_path: All Nevadans qualify by residency.

credit_unions.products_brief: Statewide Nevada CU strong in mortgages, ag lending, and northern Nevada branches.
credit_unions.blurb: Greater Nevada covers the whole Silver State and is one of its largest CU mortgage lenders, with unusual agricultural-lending depth for the rural north. Any Nevadan can join.
cons: Merged into America First Credit Union effective Oct 1, 2026, and now operates as a division of it; read member notices for account details

credit_unions.name: Service Federal Credit Union

fom.summary: Active-duty military, veterans and their families; current and former DoD employees and families; employees/members of Workplace Partners (SEGs); members of the Financial Fitness Association (free); or anyone via free American Consumer Council membership.
fom.easy_path: Anyone can join: pick the free American Consumer Council option in the application.

credit_unions.products_brief: Military-focused CU with branches in Germany, 10% deposit-rate match perks, open to all via ACC.
credit_unions.blurb: Service CU pairs deep military focus — including branches on bases in Germany — with one of the easiest open-membership paths anywhere: a free American Consumer Council membership. Its dividend-boosting direct-deposit perks reward primary banking.
pros: Free nationwide membership path via ACC
Direct-deposit rate boosts and early pay
cons: Branches limited to New England and military bases
Best perks require direct deposit relationship

credit_unions.name: St. Mary's Bank

fom.summary: Membership is open to anyone; a $5 membership share is all that's required.
fom.easy_path: Anyone can join with a $5 membership share.

credit_unions.products_brief: America's first credit union (1908), still serving New Hampshire with full-service banking.
credit_unions.blurb: St. Mary's Bank is, despite the name, a credit union — the very first one chartered in the United States, founded 1908 by Manchester millworkers. Today it's a full-service New Hampshire cooperative with a museum's worth of history and a modern product shelf. Membership is open to anyone with a $5 membership share.
pros: Historic institution with deep NH roots
credit_unions.best_for: New Hampshire residents and history buffs

credit_unions.name: Affinity Federal Credit Union

fom.summary: Employees of 2,000+ participating businesses, associations and clubs (and their immediate family/household members), and 'most everyone' by joining a participating association or club (e.g. local Chambers of Commerce, Midtown Toastmasters).
fom.easy_path: Anyone can join: a $5 one-time donation to the Affinity Foundation in the application qualifies you nationwide.
fom.join_cost: $5 share + $5 one-time donation to the Affinity Foundation if joining that way

credit_unions.products_brief: New Jersey's largest CU with open nonprofit join path, solid CDs, and full lending.
credit_unions.blurb: Affinity is New Jersey's biggest credit union and quietly one of the open-membership crowd — a small nonprofit donation at signup admits anyone. Garden State members get a dense branch network; everyone else gets competitive certificates online.
cons: Best rates often require bundled relationships
credit_unions.best_for: New Jersey households and CD shoppers

credit_unions.name: Nusenda Credit Union

fom.summary: Anyone who lives, works, worships, or attends school in most New Mexico counties (and El Paso County, TX), UNM community, and family of members.
fom.easy_path: Most New Mexicans qualify by residency.

credit_unions.products_brief: New Mexico's largest CU: statewide reach, free checking, community-lending mission.
credit_unions.blurb: Nusenda is New Mexico's flagship cooperative, open to most of the state, with free checking and a community-rewards program that funds local nonprofits based on member card swipes.

credit_unions.name: United Nations Federal Credit Union (UNFCU)

fom.summary: UN system employees, retirees, NGOs affiliated with the UN, and their families — a genuinely international field of membership.

credit_unions.products_brief: Banking for the UN community worldwide: multi-currency fluency, international wires, expat-aware service.
credit_unions.blurb: UNFCU exists for the UN's global workforce — people whose financial lives span duty stations and currencies. For members it handles international realities (wires, expat credit, overseas service) that US banks fumble; for everyone else it's admire-from-afar.

credit_unions.name: ESL Federal Credit Union

fom.summary: Live in one of 21 New York counties (incl. Monroe, Erie, Onondaga, Ontario, Wayne) AND either have a family/household member at ESL, live/work/worship/attend school in the City of Rochester, work for an eligible company or group, or join the George Eastman Museum (ESL pays for that membership). Immediate family of members also qualify.
fom.easy_path: Living in an eligible county qualifies you through the George Eastman Museum path (ESL pays for the museum membership).
fom.join_cost: $1 minimum deposit (Daily Dividend savings, opened with every membership)

credit_unions.products_brief: Rochester's dominant financial institution, born at Eastman Kodak, with annual owner dividends.
credit_unions.blurb: ESL — George Eastman's creation for Kodak workers — is now greater Rochester's leading financial institution of any kind, bank or credit union. Its annual Owners' Dividend has returned well over a hundred million dollars to members in good years.
cons: Everyday rates are average — the dividend is the kicker

credit_unions.name: Hudson Valley Credit Union

fom.summary: Anyone who lives in CT, MA, NJ, NY, PA or VT can join through the HVCU Charitable Foundation (HVCU covers the fee); also immediate family/household of members, HVCU employees, and affiliates of the Community Impact Fund or American Consumer Council.
fom.easy_path: Residents of CT, MA, NJ, NY, PA or VT can join through the HVCU Charitable Foundation; HVCU covers the fee.

credit_unions.products_brief: The Hudson Valley's leading CU with free checking, strong CDs, and broad county coverage.
credit_unions.blurb: HVCU is the Hudson Valley's financial anchor between the NYC metro and the Capital District, with certificate pricing that regularly beats downstate banks and free checking across its seven-county footprint.
pros: Competitive CD rates for New York
cons: Branch density thins at the edges

credit_unions.name: Coastal Credit Union

fom.summary: Employees of hundreds of partner employers; immediate family and household members of members; a community charter covering 25 listed North Carolina towns (e.g. Littleton, Weldon, Rocky Mount, Tarboro) plus Vance County; or anyone who joins the Coastal Credit Union Foundation as a 'Champion for Change' ($18).
fom.easy_path: Join the Coastal Credit Union Foundation as a Champion for Change ($18 contribution); open to people outside NC too.
fom.join_cost: $25 deposit to primary savings (+$18 Foundation contribution if joining via the Foundation)

credit_unions.products_brief: The Research Triangle's tech-economy CU with high-yield checking tiers and video tellers.
credit_unions.blurb: Coastal serves Raleigh-Durham's tech corridor with rate-tiered checking that rewards engagement and a pioneering video-teller branch model with extended hours. Anyone, in North Carolina or beyond, can join with an $18 Coastal Credit Union Foundation contribution.
cons: Branches concentrated in the Triangle region
Top rates require multiple relationship boxes

credit_unions.name: Truliant Federal Credit Union

fom.summary: Anyone in any U.S. state through the American Consumer Council (free); people who live, work, worship or attend school in a county near a Truliant branch; employees of partner companies; immediate family/household of members.
fom.easy_path: Anyone in the U.S. can join for free through the American Consumer Council.

credit_unions.products_brief: Piedmont-region CU across three states with free checking and small-business focus.
credit_unions.blurb: Truliant spans the Carolinas' Piedmont into Virginia with a straightforward value proposition: free checking, fair loans, and unusually attentive small-business banking for a credit union its size.
pros: Anyone can join free through the American Consumer Council

credit_unions.name: Capital Credit Union

fom.summary: Anyone who lives within 75 miles of Bismarck, Fargo, Hazen or Flasher, ND, or within 50 miles of Beulah or New Salem, ND; or has immediate family who are members living within 50 miles of Bismarck.
fom.easy_path: Bismarck-Mandan area residency qualifies you.

credit_unions.products_brief: Central North Dakota cooperative with ag lending roots and community banking basics.
credit_unions.blurb: Capital CU serves the Bismarck-Mandan region with the prairie essentials done right: free checking, ag-aware lending, and decision-makers who live in town.

credit_unions.name: General Electric Credit Union

fom.summary: Anyone who lives, works, worships or attends school in 28 listed Ohio counties (incl. Hamilton, Franklin, Montgomery) or 32 listed Kentucky counties (incl. Kenton, Jefferson), or lives/works in 5 Indiana counties (Dearborn, Franklin, Ohio, Switzerland, Union); GE Aerospace and other listed GE employees/pensioners; listed churches, school districts, TriHealth/Mercy Health and 300+ select employer groups; and family/household of members.
fom.easy_path: Tri-state Cincinnati residency qualifies you.

credit_unions.products_brief: Cincinnati-region CU with nationally competitive deposit rates and a strong rewards card.
credit_unions.blurb: GECU (the Cincinnati one) consistently posts certificate and money-market rates that make national comparison tables — unusual for a regional institution — plus free checking and a genuinely competitive rewards credit card.
pros: Deposit rates that frequently chart nationally
cons: Shares its acronym with an unrelated El Paso CU

credit_unions.name: Superior Credit Union

fom.summary: Anyone who lives, works, worships or attends school in 33 listed counties: 28 in Ohio (including Allen, Auglaize, Franklin, Hamilton, Lucas, Butler, Warren and Wood) plus Boone, Campbell and Kenton (KY), Dearborn (IN) and Monroe (MI).
fom.easy_path: Residency in its listed Ohio counties (west, central, Columbus, Cincinnati and Toledo areas) or five border counties qualifies you.

credit_unions.products_brief: Western Ohio CU repeatedly ranked among America's healthiest, with standout mortgage pricing.
credit_unions.blurb: Superior is a small-city Ohio cooperative that keeps landing on national 'best-performing credit union' lists, with mortgage and CD pricing that punches far above its Lima headquarters' weight.

credit_unions.name: Tinker Federal Credit Union

fom.summary: Tinker AFB and military personnel, employees of hundreds of partner groups, anyone who lives or works in qualifying central Oklahoma areas, and family of members.
fom.easy_path: Central Oklahoma residency or employer lists cover most OKC-area residents.

credit_unions.products_brief: Oklahoma's largest credit union, Air Force-born, with statewide-scale branches and fair pricing across the board.
credit_unions.blurb: Tinker Federal is Oklahoma's biggest cooperative, anchored to its namesake Air Force base but open to most of central Oklahoma. Members get the classic big-CU bundle: free checking, fair loans, and broad branch access.

credit_unions.name: TTCU Federal Credit Union

fom.summary: Employees, students and volunteers of 220+ selected Oklahoma schools; employees and members of affiliated groups; members, employees and volunteers of the Oklahoma PTA; members of the TTCU Cares Foundation (a $12+ donation); retirees of those groups; and immediate family/household of eligible people.
fom.easy_path: Anyone can qualify: a donation of $12 or more makes you a TTCU Cares Foundation member, which is an eligible group.
fom.join_cost: $12+ one-time TTCU Cares Foundation donation if joining that way (share deposit not stated)

credit_unions.products_brief: Tulsa's teacher-born CU, now community-wide, with free checking and education-sector perks.
credit_unions.blurb: TTCU grew from Tulsa's teachers into the city's community credit union, keeping education-sector perks while opening to the broader region. A fee-light, locally rooted alternative to Tulsa's banks.
credit_unions.best_for: Oklahoma educators and families; anyone via the TTCU Cares Foundation

credit_unions.name: OnPoint Community Credit Union

fom.summary: Live or work in one of 33 Oregon counties, or live, work, worship or go to school in Clark, Skamania, Cowlitz or Lewis County, WA; plus family of eligible people.
fom.easy_path: Broad geographic field covering most of Oregon's population.

credit_unions.products_brief: Full-service checking and savings, strong HELOC and mortgage lineup, business banking, and one of the largest branch networks in Oregon.
credit_unions.blurb: OnPoint is Oregon's largest credit union and a fixture in the Portland metro, known for branch density (including in-store locations) and consistent local service awards.
cons: Membership limited to OR and two WA counties
Savings rates middle of the pack
credit_unions.best_for: Oregonians who want a big-bank branch footprint with credit union pricing

credit_unions.name: Oregon Community Credit Union

fom.summary: Live in one of 31 listed Oregon counties or anywhere in Washington state (70-county membership area); University of Oregon students/employees/alumni association members; Bi-Mart employees/members and family; State of Oregon employees; immediate family of members.
fom.easy_path: Residency in most Oregon counties or anywhere in Washington qualifies; Bi-Mart membership is another route.

credit_unions.products_brief: Checking with no monthly fees, auto loans (a major indirect lender in the state), credit cards, and mortgages.
credit_unions.blurb: OCCU is a major auto lender in the Pacific Northwest and keeps fees low across its everyday accounts.
credit_unions.best_for: Oregon car buyers and fee-averse checking customers

credit_unions.name: PSECU

fom.summary: Relatives/household of PSECU members, affiliates of partner PA colleges/universities, employees of 1,000+ partner PA employers, or members of the Pennsylvania Recreation and Parks Society or Pennsylvania Consumer Council.
fom.easy_path: Join the Pennsylvania Recreation and Parks Society or Pennsylvania Consumer Council (association dues not stated on PSECU's page).

credit_unions.products_brief: Digital-first banking: free checking with ATM rebates, solid savings rates, low-rate credit cards and auto loans. Few branches by design.
credit_unions.blurb: PSECU runs a nearly branchless, digital-first model and passes the savings to members through ATM fee rebates and low loan rates.
pros: Strong app for a regional CU
credit_unions.best_for: Pennsylvanians comfortable with branchless digital banking

credit_unions.name: Members 1st Federal Credit Union

fom.summary: Live, work, worship, or attend school in central Pennsylvania counties, or family of a member.
fom.easy_path: Broad community charter across south-central PA.

credit_unions.products_brief: Full-service retail and business banking with 60+ branches across central Pennsylvania.
credit_unions.blurb: Members 1st pairs a dense central-PA branch network with full-service lending, making it the default community option in the Harrisburg region.
credit_unions.best_for: Central Pennsylvania households that want in-person service

credit_unions.name: Citadel Credit Union

fom.summary: Federal multiple-common-bond charter (since March 2026): residents of designated underserved areas, employees of affiliated select employee groups, association partners, and family/household of members; serves PA, DE, NJ, NY, OH, MD and WV.
fom.easy_path: Live in a designated underserved area, work for an affiliated employer group, or join through an association partner; family/household of members also qualify.

credit_unions.products_brief: High-yield savings promos, certificates that frequently top regional rate tables, mortgages, and business banking.
credit_unions.blurb: Citadel regularly posts some of the most aggressive CD and savings promo rates in the Philadelphia market.
cons: Promo rates can require new money

credit_unions.name: American Heritage Credit Union

fom.summary: Employees of 800+ workplace partners, residents of certain Philadelphia-area communities — or anyone who joins the Kids-N-Hope Foundation.
fom.easy_path: Make a one-time minimum $5 donation to the Kids-N-Hope Foundation.
fom.join_cost: $5 minimum one-time Kids-N-Hope Foundation donation (share deposit not stated)

credit_unions.products_brief: Competitive money market and CD rates, free checking options, auto and home lending.
credit_unions.blurb: American Heritage is one of the lesser-known anyone-can-join credit unions: a small one-time donation to its children's health foundation opens membership from anywhere in the US.
pros: Anyone can join via foundation donation
Strong CD and money market rates
credit_unions.best_for: Rate shoppers anywhere in the US looking for an easy-membership CU

credit_unions.name: Navigant Credit Union

fom.summary: Community credit union: 'Anyone may join, subject to proper verification.'
fom.easy_path: Open membership - anyone may join, subject to verification.

credit_unions.products_brief: Checking, savings, CDs, mortgages, and business lending with the largest credit union branch footprint in Rhode Island.
credit_unions.blurb: Navigant is Rhode Island's largest credit union, over a century old, with deep roots in the state's mill-town communities. Membership is open to anyone, subject to verification.
credit_unions.best_for: Rhode Islanders who want a local full-service institution

credit_unions.name: Founders Federal Credit Union

fom.summary: Employees of hundreds of partner companies and residents of certain South Carolina counties and nearby NC areas.
fom.easy_path: Broad employer and community lists across upstate South Carolina.

credit_unions.products_brief: Low-rate auto loans and credit cards, free checking, branches across upstate SC and into North Carolina.
credit_unions.blurb: Founders is a Carolinas mainstay known for very low loan rates and a no-frills, member-first culture.
cons: Eligibility tied to SC/NC areas and employers
credit_unions.best_for: Carolina borrowers prioritizing rate over app polish

credit_unions.name: Black Hills Federal Credit Union

fom.summary: Live, work, worship, or attend school in South Dakota, or live/work/worship/attend school/volunteer in Yellowstone or Big Horn counties, Montana.
fom.easy_path: Statewide South Dakota community charter plus Yellowstone and Big Horn counties, MT.

credit_unions.products_brief: Checking, savings, ag and business lending, mortgages, and auto loans across South Dakota.
credit_unions.blurb: Black Hills FCU is South Dakota's largest credit union, with statewide eligibility and a lending book that reflects the state's ranching and small-business economy.
pros: Anyone in South Dakota can join
credit_unions.best_for: South Dakotans, especially ranchers and small-business owners

credit_unions.name: Eastman Credit Union

fom.summary: Employees of Eastman Chemical and hundreds of partner employers, plus residents of specific TN/VA/TX counties.
fom.easy_path: Broad employer list and Tri-Cities-area community eligibility.

credit_unions.products_brief: Famous for paying large annual member dividends, plus low loan rates, free checking, and strong CDs.
credit_unions.blurb: Eastman CU routinely returns extraordinary annual bonus dividends to members — frequently among the largest payouts of any US credit union — on top of already competitive rates.
credit_unions.best_for: Tri-Cities residents who want a CU that literally pays you back

credit_unions.name: ORNL Federal Credit Union

fom.summary: Live, work, worship, or attend school in 19 East Tennessee counties.
fom.easy_path: Broad East Tennessee community charter.
fom.join_cost: $1 deposit to open the Membership Account

credit_unions.products_brief: Full-service banking born out of the Oak Ridge National Laboratory community: checking, mortgages, auto loans, and business accounts.
credit_unions.blurb: Founded for Manhattan Project-era lab workers, ORNL FCU now serves a 19-county swath of East Tennessee with full-service banking.

credit_unions.name: University Federal Credit Union

fom.summary: UT Austin students/alumni/staff, employees of hundreds of partner groups, and residents of the Austin and Galveston areas.
fom.easy_path: Join through the American Consumer Council for free (UFCU handles enrollment).
fom.join_cost: $1 minimum deposit to the basic savings account

credit_unions.products_brief: Free checking, strong auto lending, mortgages tuned to the Austin market, and university-adjacent perks.
credit_unions.blurb: UFCU is Austin's hometown credit union, with deep University of Texas ties and a big share of the local auto loan market.

credit_unions.name: Credit Human

fom.summary: Live, work, worship or attend school in the San Antonio or New Orleans service areas; employees/members of partner organizations; students of partner schools; military, veterans and dependents; family/household of members; or anyone in the U.S. via the American Consumer Council (Louisiana residents use the Louisiana Consumer Council).
fom.easy_path: Join the American Consumer Council through Credit Human at no cost, from anywhere in the U.S.
fom.join_cost: $5 share deposit (ACC fee paid by Credit Human)

credit_unions.products_brief: Checking and savings, CDs that often lead Texas rate tables, and a national manufactured-housing lending program.
credit_unions.blurb: Credit Human (formerly SACU) pairs San Antonio retail banking with one of the country's largest manufactured-home lending operations.
credit_unions.best_for: San Antonio savers and manufactured-home buyers nationwide

credit_unions.name: American Airlines Credit Union

fom.summary: Employees and retirees of the air transportation industry and their family members.
fom.easy_path: Any air-transport-industry connection — airlines, airports, aviation contractors — qualifies.

credit_unions.products_brief: Priority checking, strong CD ladder options, auto loans, and branches in dozens of US airports.
credit_unions.blurb: AA Credit Union serves the whole air transportation industry, not just American Airlines, with branches inside major airports and consistently solid CD rates.
credit_unions.best_for: Anyone working in or retired from aviation

credit_unions.name: Goldenwest Credit Union

fom.summary: Live, work, worship, volunteer or attend school in Weber or Salt Lake County or select areas of Cache, Davis, Utah and Washington counties (UT), select areas of 13 Idaho counties and Malheur County, OR; plus school, employer/association affiliations and family of members.
fom.easy_path: Community eligibility in Weber/Salt Lake counties and parts of northern Utah, Idaho and eastern Oregon.

credit_unions.products_brief: Checking, savings, auto and RV loans, mortgages, plus in-house insurance services.
credit_unions.blurb: Goldenwest, founded by railroad workers in 1936, now serves most of Utah with full banking plus an unusual in-house insurance agency.
credit_unions.best_for: Utah households that want banking and insurance under one roof

credit_unions.name: EastRise Credit Union (formerly New England Federal Credit Union)

fom.summary: Employees of select employer groups (e.g. State of Vermont, Vermont colleges and nonprofits, IBM in ME/MA/RI/VT/parts of CT), members of listed organizations (e.g. Vermont General Assembly, Washington Electric Cooperative), and family/household of members, or anyone through a complimentary American Consumer Council membership.
fom.easy_path: Complimentary American Consumer Council membership (EastRise pays the first-year fee) makes anyone eligible.

credit_unions.products_brief: Vermont's dominant mortgage lender among CUs, plus checking, savings, and auto loans.
credit_unions.blurb: EastRise — the combined NEFCU and VSECU under a new name — is Vermont's largest credit union and a leading mortgage lender in the state. Anyone can join through a complimentary American Consumer Council membership.
pros: Anyone can join via a free ACC membership

credit_unions.name: Langley Federal Credit Union

fom.summary: Open to anyone, with no military, residency, or occupational requirements.
fom.easy_path: No eligibility requirements: anyone can join with a $5 opening deposit.

credit_unions.products_brief: High-yield savings tiers, frequent CD specials, free checking, and Hampton Roads branch coverage.
credit_unions.blurb: Born alongside NASA's Langley laboratory, Langley FCU is a Hampton Roads anchor that frequently posts strong savings and CD specials. Membership is now open to anyone, with no military, residency, or occupational requirement.

credit_unions.name: Apple Federal Credit Union

fom.summary: Anyone who lives, works, worships, or attends school in select Northern Virginia counties, plus school-community ties.
fom.easy_path: Broad Northern Virginia community eligibility.

credit_unions.products_brief: Education-rooted CU with strong CD rates, free checking, and student/teacher-friendly products.
credit_unions.blurb: Founded by Fairfax County educators, Apple FCU now serves much of Northern Virginia and is a regular on CD rate leaderboards.
cons: No relation to the tech company (worth saying out loud)

credit_unions.name: WSECU

fom.summary: Anyone who lives, works, or worships in Washington state, plus relatives of eligible people and students at CWU, Evergreen, UW, or WSU.
fom.easy_path: Statewide Washington eligibility.

credit_unions.products_brief: Free checking, competitive credit cards, mortgages, and branches across Washington.
credit_unions.blurb: Washington State Employees Credit Union long ago opened to all Washingtonians and is now one of the state's most accessible full-service CUs.
cons: BECU overshadows it in Puget Sound

credit_unions.name: STCU

fom.summary: Live, work, worship, or attend college in Washington state, North Idaho (8 counties) or Eastern Oregon (14 counties); relatives of eligible people; or employees of STCU Community Business Partners.
fom.easy_path: Broad Inland Northwest eligibility.
fom.join_cost: $10 one-time membership fee (adults 18+), $5 for students 18+; no fee if you join online, are under 18, or are an employed educator

credit_unions.products_brief: Free checking, strong auto and home lending, and the dominant branch network in the Spokane region.
credit_unions.blurb: Spokane Teachers Credit Union outgrew its name decades ago and is now the Inland Northwest's largest financial cooperative.

credit_unions.name: Pioneer Appalachia Federal Credit Union

fom.summary: Live, work, worship, attend school or volunteer in eligible communities (approved census tracts) across West Virginia, Virginia, Maryland, Kentucky, Ohio and Pennsylvania; immediate family of members; or Volunteer Members of the WVSSPA.
fom.easy_path: Check your address: eligibility is set by approved census tracts in six states, centered on West Virginia.

credit_unions.products_brief: Checking, savings, auto loans, personal loans, and mortgages for the Charleston, WV metro.
credit_unions.blurb: Pioneer Appalachia (formerly Pioneer WV) is the Charleston area's homegrown credit union, serving state-capital-region households since 1936.

credit_unions.name: Landmark Credit Union

fom.summary: Live or work in Southern and Northeastern Wisconsin, or Lake and McHenry Counties in Illinois; immediate family of eligible people; businesses located in those areas.
fom.easy_path: Broad two-state regional eligibility.

credit_unions.products_brief: Wisconsin's largest CU: premium checking with high-yield tiers, mortgages, auto loans, and 35+ branches.
credit_unions.blurb: Landmark is Wisconsin's largest credit union, known for a high-yield premium checking account and a dense Milwaukee-area branch network.

credit_unions.name: Summit Credit Union

fom.summary: Open charter: anyone can become a member.
fom.easy_path: Open charter: anyone can join with a $1 savings deposit.

credit_unions.products_brief: Full-service banking with a financial-wellness bent: free checking, strong mortgage operation, and money-coaching programs.
credit_unions.blurb: Summit is Madison's hometown credit union and one of Wisconsin's largest mortgage lenders, with an unusually deep financial-education program.
pros: Open charter: anyone can join with a $1 deposit

credit_unions.name: Blue Federal Credit Union

fom.summary: Military/civilian personnel of partner organizations, residents of Wyoming and Colorado communities — or anyone who joins the Blue Foundation.
fom.easy_path: A one-time $5 donation to the Blue Foundation makes anyone in the US eligible.

credit_unions.products_brief: High-yield accounts that frequently appear on national rate lists, plus checking, auto loans, and mortgages.
credit_unions.blurb: Blue FCU, born at Warren Air Force Base, is one of the cheapest anyone-can-join credit unions in the country: a $5 foundation donation opens nationwide membership, and its CD and savings specials often rank nationally.
pros: Anyone can join for a $5 donation
credit_unions.best_for: Rate shoppers anywhere wanting the cheapest open-membership path
